g.text: HOST EVENT SOURCES — the only layer that differs between VS Code, IntelliJ and Neovim

g.title: reconcile
g.text: signal 1 insert shape + signal 2 command intercept

g.title: h_clip
g.text: VS Code never reads the clipboard;
its signal 3 is the count reconciler

g.title: tx
g.text: relative paths · one inline content cap (64 KB)

g.title: h_git
g.text: built-in API · Git4Idea · external — may be absent
every git.event carrying a sha is labelled with its
repository's ROOT-COMMIT sha, derived once per
repository at wiring setup. Omitted — never null,
never guessed — on a shallow clone or any failure

g.title: h_prov
g.text: ONE watcher on the DIRECTORY, not one per file, and
Callbacks enqueue a basename and return —
no I/O, no hashing, no parsing on the callback

g.title: drain
g.text: every 100 entries and at dispose — never on the
watcher callback. An unchanged file is NOT
re-emitted. Own files excluded by name.
A LOCAL read failure (EACCES/EIO) is a fact about
THIS machine, not the partner's file: emit nothing.
An unreadable chain ⇒ state unparseable, with all
Never rename, rewrite or delete a foreign file.

g.title: explain
g.text: one mark · 2 s window · a Set of up to
64 distinct paths, not a single slot —
so one git pull explains every file it
KEPT, not a bridge: it is the only
mitigation for a solo, 1.x or unenrolled
CHAIN POSITION. No student ref, no key,
no git author, no path outside .provenance/

g.title: polic
g.text: resolved once from the course-signed manifest
one lookup in a frozen map —

g.title: drop
g.text: dropped at the ONE choke point —
and BEFORE chaining, so it consumes no seq.
Dropping after would leave a gap that
validation check 4 reads as a deletion.

g.title: buf
g.text: the firehose must not block the editor

g.title: roll
g.text: ROLLING SEAL — rewritten, not written once
signed by that session's OWN ephemeral key.
At session start · on every checkpoint · once more at
dispose, and ONLY that last one carries final: true.
The git path never runs seal — this IS its seal.
at session start, on every checkpoint,
and once more at dispose — always AFTER
the peer drain, so the observations land in
the bytes this seal is about to commit to
a PAIR commit — a signature and the payload
it covers only mean anything together
